traits.central_spine_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Ferocactus wislizeni: 'Spines 16-25(-29) per areole, central spines and larger radial spines dull pink, gray, or tan; smallest spines per areole white, slender, often bristlelike, less than 1 mm diam., strongly contrasting with central spines'; it says nothing of greying. With three colours named for the centrals, the colour was measured: the median of the non-green pixels inside the spine cover of seven iNaturalist photographs (imagekit batch inat-cacti-2026-10-19, photos 1, 2, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11 in key order), the brighter three quarters of each, then the median of the photos: RGB 145, 114, 94, a grey-brown with a pink cast. Until 2026-10-19 the centrals were a bright red by hand, greying over 25 years.

traits.spine_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Ferocactus wislizeni: 'Spines 16-25(-29) per areole, central spines and larger radial spines dull pink, gray, or tan; smallest spines per areole white, slender, often bristlelike, less than 1 mm diam., strongly contrasting with central spines'; it says nothing of greying. The radial set here is the white bristles; their white by hand from the word.

traits.fruit_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 337, Ferocactus wislizeni: fruit ovoid, yellow, to 5 cm long.

generator.params.sun_tilt.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986) p. 195: Ferocactus wislizenii stems lean 17 degrees toward the equator at 33 degrees north.

traits.tubercle_relief.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 337, Ferocactus wislizeni: barely tuberculate, the ribs with at most a swelling under each areole.

traits.flower_colour.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 337, Ferocactus wislizeni: flowers funnelform, yellow to yellowish orange to red (yellowish orange, the middle of the words), 4 to 5 cm long and wide; fruit ovoid, yellow, to 5 cm long (typical a little short of it, by hand).

traits.flower_size_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 337, Ferocactus wislizeni: flowers funnelform, yellow to yellowish orange to red (yellowish orange, the middle of the words), 4 to 5 cm long and wide; fruit ovoid, yellow, to 5 cm long (typical a little short of it, by hand).

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) p. 337, Ferocactus wislizeni: flowers funnelform, yellow to yellowish orange to red (yellowish orange, the middle of the words), 4 to 5 cm long and wide; fruit ovoid, yellow, to 5 cm long (typical a little short of it, by hand).

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 3, 1922, p. 128): ribs numerous, often 25, about 3 cm high; areoles 2 to 3 cm apart, large and brown-felted; radial spines thread-like to needle-like, the longest 5 cm; several centrals, one much stouter, flattened and strongly hooked.

traits.ribs.note: FEIS's review of Ferocactus wislizeni (Matthews 1994): 20 to 28 ribs; Britton and Rose's usual count is 25.

traits.stem_diameter_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Ferocactus wislizeni: stems 19-100(-300) × (20-)36-65(-100) cm, so 36 to 65 cm thick, 20 to 100 at the extremes. FEIS's review (Matthews 1994) gives 45 to 83 cm, which stood here until round 5. The stem's widening over 60 cm of height, set by hand until then, now comes from the family's rule on its globose genus.

traits.radial_spines.note: FEIS's review of Ferocactus wislizeni (Matthews 1994): 12 to 20 radial spines.

traits.central_spines.note: FEIS's review of Ferocactus wislizeni (Matthews 1994): 4 central spines, the larger ones 3.8 to 5 cm long.

traits.central_spine_length_m.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001), Ferocactus wislizeni: central spines 4, in a cross, 8 to 10 cm long, the lowest flattened, stoutest and often hooked. FEIS (Matthews 1994) gives 3.8 to 5 cm for the larger centrals; photographs show hooks as long as the radials or longer, as Anderson has it.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a single barrel that grows from a spiny ball to a stout column 1 to 1.6 m tall (rarely 3 m) and 45 to 60 cm across, leaning toward the south as it grows (the compass barrel). A ring of orange to red flowers in late summer and yellow fruit that stays on the crown for months. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: about half a metre by 30 years, a metre by 60. Wide tolerances.

generator.params.flowers.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986), ch. 5: most cacti flower in a ring near the stem tip, one flower to an areole made about a year before, with a few areoles in the ring left unused; 20 here, for the 21 to 28 ribs, flowers and fruit together.

appearance.bodies.stem.spines.central.le.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001), Ferocactus wislizeni: the four centrals, in a cross, 8 to 10 cm long; 8 cm here for the three beside the hooked one, as for it.

generator.params.crown_rings.note: Photographs of the crown (iNaturalist, credits in plantgen-claude project-files/cacti/photo-credits-2026-10-15.md): this year's ring of buds and flowers sits inside a ring of last year's yellow fruit, which stay on the plant, so two rings, the older about 14 degrees farther down the dome (by eye). This year's ring therefore holds buds and flowers only, the fruit being the older ring's. Since 2026-10-18 neither ring draws buds or fruit all year: every place in this year's ring is a bud before it opens, a flower in its months and fruit after them (the family's rule, bud_share and fruit_share 0, where its months are stated), and the older ring holds its fruit in its fruiting months.

generator.params.ring_step.note: By eye from the same photographs: the older ring of fruit sits just below this year's.

appearance.bodies.stem.ribs.fibonacci.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986), pp. 123-124: Ferocactus rib counts cluster on Fibonacci numbers; in F. acanthodes 51% of plants had one, 21 the commonest. Half the stems here keep to the Fibonacci number in the count.

appearance.bodies.stem.ribs.lean.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986), pp. 121 and 125: tubercle rows lean about 30 degrees from vertical, so a Fibonacci-ribbed Ferocactus winds slowly round the stem, left-handed in about half the plants and right-handed in the rest; other stems stand straight.

appearance.bodies.stem.areoles.apex_wool.note: Gibson and Nobel, The Cactus Primer (1986), ch. 5: the young areoles' trichomes crowd at the apex into a woolly mat, in barrel cacti more than 4 cm thick. 1.5 cm here, less than that, because in photographs this species' apex shows mostly spines over its wool (thickness by eye).

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: green skin with 20 to 28 sharp ribs and chins under the areoles; a dense cover of white bristly radials, three reddish cross-shaped centrals and one broad, flattened central hooked like a fishhook, greying with age. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact. Since round 5 (2026-10-19) it ends at the age the plant reaches the middle of the flora's usual height (Flora of North America's 19-100 cm, so about 0.6 m, at 35 years on its height curve), so its oldest keyframe, the one rendered and checked, is a typical plant rather than one of 100 years and 1.5 m.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-19), Ferocactus wislizeni: stems usually leaning southward in adulthood, depressed-spheric to ovoid-cylindric, 19-100(-300) × (20-)36-65(-100) cm; the usual heights 19 to 100 cm, rarely to 3 m. Until round 5 a model estimate of 0.6 to 1.6 m.

traits.height_max_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2808252), as no source read gives it.

traits.woodiness.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2808252), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2808252), as no source read gives it.

traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles (1942), Echinocactus wislizeni (Ferocactus wislizeni): July to September in Arizona. FEIS (Matthews 1994) gives a few flowers in late spring and most in July to September, and the Flora of North America (vol. 4, read on eFloras 2026-10-18) late summer, sometimes into fall. Until 2026-10-18 a model estimate of the same months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA-NPN Nature's Notebook phenometrics for Ferocactus wislizeni (species 867, fetched 2026-10-18; the method of the phenology work of 2026-10-14 without its Pacific Northwest filter): 652 individual-year spans with ripe fruit at 56 sites, nearly all in Arizona; the months with at least a third of the busiest month's days, September to April, as the fruit stays on the plant through the winter (FEIS: mule deer eat it mostly in fall and winter; the Flora of North America: Ferocactus fruit long persistent). Until 2026-10-18 a model estimate, January and September to December.

traits.fruit_width_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Ferocactus wislizeni: fruit bright yellow, 35 to 60 by 18 to 40 mm, thick walled.
